Hi Anna — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we stay aligned.

What we heard (please correct if anything off):
- Workload: conversational triage + clinical summarization for patient messages.
- Expected blended volume: ~50M tokens/month on average, with short-term peaks to ~200M in campaign windows.
- Procurement timeline: ~6–8 weeks (internal legal + security review).
- Target commercial posture: looking for a sustainable long-term price; early pilot could accept a higher unit cost if we get SLA/observability.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the average + peak tokens above?
2) Ballpark monthly budget range to reserve for LLM inference during pilot (gives us a price band to work within).
3) Any mandatory compliance docs beyond SOC2 (e.g., BAA, data residency)?

How we can help now:
- I attached a short benchmark (redwood-token-benchmark-2025.xlsx) that summarizes our internal $/1M token comparisons vs popular hosts and self-hosted options.
- Internally we’ll surface a few pricing scenarios vs OpenAI/Anthropic and a commitment-based Dedicated offer.
- Proposed next step: 30m follow-up next week to lock target $/1M and pilot commit level — any days/times that work?

Attachments: redwood-token-benchmark-2025.xlsx (summary), procurement-checklist.pdf (redwood-side checklist)

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks, Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. Quick confirmations and a few clarifying notes: 

Confirmed volumes:
- Average: ~50M tokens/month (we expect that within Q4 once rolling out to 30% of users)
- Peak: up to ~200M tokens during marketing/feature pushes (short windows)

Budget range for pilot/proof-of-concept:
- Running internal numbers: we can earmark $2k–$6k/month for the initial pilot phase (90 days) depending on what’s included (support, SLA, observability). 

Target unit economics:
- We’re aiming for an eventual long-term target of roughly $25–$40 per 1M tokens — recognizes OpenAI/Anthropic list prices but wants better predictability and lower tail latency/SLA for production.

Compliance/Procurement:
- SOC2 is required; BAA may be necessary (we’ll confirm with legal). Data residency: US only.
- Procurement is on a 6–8 week cadence; I’ve looped procurement email for visibility.

Next step: happy to do a follow-up next week. I’m available Thu afternoon or Fri morning PST. Also would like a short one-pager that maps Redwood pricing vs OpenAI/Anthropic vs self-hosted (one table) — that helps my finance team.

—Anna

Karthik / Laura — quick internal note before we reply to Anna with a clean one-pager and pilot proposal. Below are our working benchmark numbers (per 1M tokens) and suggested pilot posture: 

Benchmarks (blended inference equivalent, rounded):
- OpenAI (hosted managed): $20 / 1M tokens (public list, varies by model)
- Anthropic (hosted managed): $18 / 1M tokens
- Typical cloud-hosted open-model (self-managed, unoptimized): $12–$15 / 1M (no observability/SLA)
- Redwood Hosted (managed, multi-tenant): $12 / 1M (target at scale; promotional for pilots)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, commit): $7–$9 / 1M depending on commit/quantization profile
- On-prem / Air-gapped (customer-managed infra with Redwood Private): $9–$14 / 1M depending on HW and ops footprint

Notes / assumptions:
- Benchmarks above assume 8k–10k tokens/session distribution and average sequence lengths we saw on the call.
- Peak windows will change effective unit cost; for short spikes we recommend a burst policy (mix of hosted + Dedicated fallback) to avoid huge overages.

Suggested ask to Anna:
1) Offer a 90-day pilot at $12 / 1M with a 50M tokens/month soft commit; this gives them a predictable band and we keep room to price down with higher committed volumes.
2) Provide a line-item one-pager that shows OpenAI/Anthropic list prices vs our Hosted vs Dedicated commit scenarios.
3) Include SOC2 + optional BAA in the one-pager and flag data-residency options.

Attachments to prepare: pricing-proposal-pulsehealth-v1.pdf (covers pilot economics + SLA), one-pager table for finance.

If that looks good I’ll draft the reply and attach the one-pager.

—Ben
